A.title: Exploring KokoroSharp: A New Local, Cross-Platform TTS Engine in C#
A.body: I came across a post from early 2025 about KokoroSharp, a local text-to-speech engine written in C# that's cross-platform and available via NuGet. The author was motivated by a new high-performance audio model called Kokoro and developed this TTS engine, describing it as beginner-friendly yet flexible. The source code is open on GitHub, and example usage includes loading a model and selecting a voice named "af_heart." While the original poster was also working on an offline AI voice chat app nearing release, detailed performance metrics or hardware requirements for KokoroSharp weren't provided. For those interested in offline speech synthesis or integrating TTS with local LLMs, what do you think are the practical challenges or opportunities with this engine? Has anyone explored KokoroSharp or similar local TTS solutions in C# or other languages?

B.title: Is KokoroSharp TTS Ready for Fully Offline AI Voice Chat Projects?
B.body:
I came across a post from early 2025 where the author was nearly finished (about 90%) with a fully offline AI voice chat app. They pivoted to build KokoroSharp, a local, cross-platform TTS engine, after a new high-performance audio model called Kokoro was released. 

The question that comes to mind is whether KokoroSharp, given its development context and near-completion status, is mature enough for offline AI voice chat projects. The source doesn’t provide detailed performance metrics or stability info, so it’s unclear how well it integrates or runs in real-world offline scenarios.

Has anyone experimented with KokoroSharp in offline voice chat setups? What are the practical trade-offs or limitations you encountered, especially regarding latency, voice quality, or platform compatibility?
